name: ballxcohort
description: Deep learning reportedly classifies B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells at 99 to 100% accuracy, but almost always within a single cohort. ballxcohort provides the single-cell harmonization pipeline that renders a full-field source cohort into the format of an external single-cell cohort, the leakage-controlled splits that make the comparison auditable, and the evaluation code for two deployment regimes. It supports three findings: the in-cohort task is saturated, since a randomly initialized network reaches 98.6% accuracy; fine-tune-and-deploy collapses to near chance across cohorts because "normal" denotes benign hematogones in one cohort and mature lymphocytes in the other, and the collapse survives freezing the encoder and withholding target labels; and a frozen in-domain foundation encoder adapted with a few local labels recovers cross-cohort performance. No image data or model weights are redistributed.
